subtype: Approach: staying alone and waiting for others to come [Pitfall]
passage: I'm Ira. When I started at the new school, I sat alone at lunch every day, holding my tiffin, hoping somebody would say 'Come and sit here.' Nobody did. I looked at the door and my tiffin in turn. Later I found out what the class thought: Bhupen told me they'd assumed I liked being alone, because I never looked up. But I looked up. I just never smiled. By Thursday my throat was tight and I ate only half my lunch. Each day was longer than the last. Waiting felt safe, because nobody could say no, but nothing changed either.

qa.q: What did Ira hold while sitting alone at lunch?
What was Ira feeling by Thursday, and what shows it?
qa.a: Ira felt lonely and sad; the tight throat and half-eaten lunch show it. 😔

qa.q: What alternative approach could Ira try, and why?
qa.a: Ira could smile and say hello to one classmate, or ask the teacher to pair Ira with a friendly buddy. A small step from Ira would give others a sign that company is wanted.

qa.q: How did the class see Ira?
qa.a: The class assumed that Ira liked being alone because Ira never seemed to look up, so they did not go over to Ira.

grounding: Ira sits alone hoping for an invitation, classmates assume it is a choice and stay away, and each day feels lonelier.
